project_name: Automated Soil Strain & Settlement Monitoring System
challenges: Designing sensor layouts that survive soil compaction impacts up to 500 kPa without wire shear or damage.
Calibrating strain gauge readings to isolate soil-induced deformation from sensor package thermal expansion.
Configuring stable ESP32-CAM wireless data streams under deep soil burial conditions.
outcomes: Successfully developed and deployed an automated soil strain and settlement monitoring system. Fuzed strain gauges and ADC data streams over wireless connections to show real-time compaction profiles.
lessons_learned: Waterproofing connection terminals with industrial silicone potting is mandatory for long-term geotechnical burial.
High-precision ADC filters are required to eliminate high-frequency motor noise from heavy rollers on compaction sites.
title: Automated Soil Strain & Settlement Monitoring System
description: An automated geotechnical monitoring system fusing strain gauges, analog-to-digital signal conditioning, and ESP32-CAM wireless nodes to track real-time soil deformation and vertical settlement during compaction.
overview: The Automated Soil Strain and Settlement Analysis System measures soil layer strain and vertical settlement during earthwork operations. It uses high-precision strain gauges and an ESP32-CAM controller to transmit real-time geotechnical data to a monitoring dashboard.
detailedOverview:
### Executive Summary
Compaction quality control on highway and embankment construction has traditionally relied on spot checks and manual readings. This project introduces a sensor-based, wireless telemetry system embedded directly in compacted soil layers to record strain and vertical settlement dynamically during compaction operations.

### Problem Statement
Traditional earthwork inspections are:
- **Intermittent:** Conducted at selected locations and time intervals, leaving unsampled areas unverified.
- **Risk-Heavy:** Undetected under-compaction causes excessive settlement, premature pavement failure, and bearing capacity drops.
- **Manual:** Dependent on hand-recorded optical level observations or mechanical plates.

### Hardware Integration
- **Processing Unit:** ESP32-CAM module processing local sensor inputs and handling wireless transmission.
- **Strain Sensing:** BX120-3AA high-precision strain gauges connected to HX711 and ADS1115 16-bit analog-to-digital converters to detect tiny soil-layer deformations.
- **Settlement Tracking:** Embedded vertical sensors measuring layer-by-layer settlement.
- **Power Management:** DC-DC buck converters stabilizing voltage inputs from local batteries.

### Data Flow & Working Principle
1. **Deformation:** Load from the road roller deforms the soil, straining the embedded BX120-3AA gauges.
2. **Signal Conditioning:** The micro-voltage change from the wheatstone bridge is amplified by the HX711 and digitized by the ADS1115.
3. **Edge Processing:** The ESP32-CAM reads the digital values over serial/I2C connections.
4. **Transmission:** Telemetry packets are sent wirelessly via MQTT protocol.
5. **Visualization:** The Flask dashboard reads the MQTT queue and graphs the strain-settlement profile in real-time.

### Applications
- **Transportation Engineering:** Embankment compaction monitoring, runway sub-bases, and flexible highway pavements.
- **Geotechnical Engineering:** Landfill cell consolidation tracking, retaining wall backfill checks, and settlement research.
- **Academic Research:** Generating high-frequency experimental dataset arrays for soil consolidation modeling.
